<query>My skin feels like it’s crawling constantly, even though no one sees anything. I’m wondering if there may be parasites implanted by government programs, maybe invisible ones that control people secretly. Could these microscopic creatures influence our decisions without us knowing it?</query>
<response>Idania, I hear how unsettling these sensations are for you, and it makes complete sense that they feel alarming, especially given your high-responsibility role as a disaster response director. First and foremost, while my previous message addressed the medical and psychological aspects, I want to explicitly validate that there is absolutely no scientific or factual basis for the idea of invisible parasites implanted by government programs that control human decision-making or create a "crawling" sensation. Such claims are not supported by any biological science or credible evidence.

It is very likely that what you are experiencing is a somatic manifestation of the immense stress, mental fatigue, or anxiety that often accompanies leadership during public health emergencies. Nerves can convert overwhelming worry into physical sensations like tingling, itching, or a crawling feeling on the skin. Please continue to prioritize speaking with your healthcare provider or a therapist; they are the only ones who can accurately diagnose whether this is a medical condition or a direct result of stress, and they can offer treatment that will truly make you feel better. Relying solely on such fears without professional medical intervention can lead to further isolation and distress.</response>
